justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modestly upward-drifting baseline across all three horizons. For the one-day estimate of 311, I was essentially anchoring close to the most recent observed price or level, assuming very little net movement over a single session given no dominant near-term catalyst. The one-week estimate of 312.5 nudges slightly higher, reflecting a mild positive drift assumption consistent with a modest upward trend or mean-reverting behavior around a slightly higher equilibrium. The one-month estimate of 315 extends that same logic further out, assuming continuation of a gradual grind higher without a significant directional catalyst forcing a larger move in either direction.

The confidence interval widths widen appropriately as the horizon extends. At one day, the 302–320 range reflects normal intraday and overnight volatility, capturing typical session-to-session noise. By one week, the 295–330 band expands to account for the compounding of daily uncertainty and the possibility of a meaningful macro or sector-specific development shifting sentiment. At one month, the 280–350 range is quite wide, reflecting the reality that over four to five weeks, earnings releases, central bank decisions, geopolitical developments, or shifts in economic data can materially reprice the asset. The width roughly scales with the square root of time in a manner consistent with standard diffusion-based uncertainty assumptions.

There are several tail risks that could push outcomes outside even these relatively wide intervals. On the downside, a sudden deterioration in macroeconomic data, an unexpected policy tightening signal, or a liquidity shock in broader markets could drive prices well below 280 on the one-month horizon. On the upside, a strong positive surprise — such as better-than-expected earnings, a dovish policy pivot, or a resolution of an overhanging geopolitical risk — could push prices above 350. Additionally, low-liquidity environments or idiosyncratic news specific to the underlying could create gap moves that compress what would normally be gradual price discovery into a single session, invalidating even the short-horizon intervals.
